findings.claim: Total area of the walled Terezín Main Fortress (Hlavní pevnost / Große Festung) enclosing the ghetto town
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: Single authoritative primary measurement directly observed in session (UNESCO Tentative List #1561, inner defense perimeter 3,040 m; total 18th-century fortress land purchase ~400 ha; Small Fortress ~2.5 ha). Corroborated in scale by Adler's 335,056 m² (33.51 ha) Jewish settlement footprint within the walled fortress.

findings.claim: Total surface area of the Jewish settlement/ghetto within Terezín and usable inmate living quarters area
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: 335,056 m² total settlement area (~42% built up, ~16% courtyards, ~42% streets/public spaces/gardens) and ~95,000 m² living space trace primarily to H. G. Adler (Ch. 11 "Housing"), cited by later scholarship including Anna Hájková. Independently cross-checked by Vojtěch Blodig (Památník Terezín), who reports 1.6 m² average living space per prisoner at the ~58,500 Sept 1942 peak (~93,600 m² implied).

findings.claim: Pre-war / pre-ghetto population of Terezín garrison town (civilians plus military garrison)
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: Beit Theresienstadt, Key Documents (Martha Glass edition), and Vojtěch Blodig cite ~7,000 total (roughly half civilian, half military); Key Documents specifies ~3,700 civilian residents resettled by July 1942, and Adler / Lederer detail ~3,700 civilians + ~3,500 soldiers (~7,200 total).

findings.claim: Peak simultaneous inmate population inside Terezín ghetto in mid-September 1942
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: EHRI Document Blog (Daily Orders) and Beit Theresienstadt report 58,491 (16 September 1942); Susanne Wurm reports 58,497 (18 September 1942); Vojtěch Blodig rounds to ~58,500. The 6-person difference reflects daily registration updates in mid-September 1942. Note: EHRI archival unit https://portal.ehri-project.eu/units/cz-002195~pt-3941 is an unrelated concert program (PT 3941), NOT a demographic figure.

findings.claim: Peak monthly death toll inside Terezín ghetto (September 1942)
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: Exact monthly figure 3,941 corroborated by EHRI Document Blog (Daily Orders), Beit Theresienstadt, and H. G. Adler.

findings.claim: Children who died directly inside the Terezín ghetto
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: Both David, Ebert, & Kuntz (2022, Karger peer-reviewed article) and Penn State / Unizin (*Terezín and 'The Last Cyclist'*, citing Nazi records) report 400 children died inside Terezín; Czech university scholarship (Masaryk University) likewise cites ~400. Major institutional summaries (USHMM, Yad Vashem, Památník Terezín) typically omit a separate in-ghetto child mortality sub-total and focus on ~15,000 total children and 7,590 deported children.

findings.claim: Children deported east from Terezín and number of those deportees who survived
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: Památník Terezín reports 7,590 youngest child prisoners deported east with 142 survivors. Penn State / Unizin reports >7,500 children deported east with 245 alive at war's end (some secondary/academic tallies cite 242). The 142 vs. 242–245 gap reflects cohort/age definitions (youngest 7,590 cohort vs. broader >7,500 child deportees) and post-war registry cutoffs.

findings.claim: Children under age 15 alive inside Terezín at liberation (May 1945)
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: Exact figure 1,633 traces to H. G. Adler (Ch. "Welfare"); David, Ebert, & Kuntz (2022, Karger) round to ~1,600. Roughly half were long-term ghetto inmates and the remainder arrived via late-war evacuation transports in April–May 1945.

findings.claim: Live births inside the Terezín ghetto (1941–1945)
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: H. G. Adler (Ch. 16 "Health Conditions") explicitly writes that figures vary between 205 and 209, possibly reaching 230 (Gonda Redlich's diary/internal records cite 207); David, Ebert, & Kuntz (2022, Karger) document Franz Bass's obstetric records (~207–230 births alongside ~350 forced abortions). Note: SS authorities falsely claimed 300–400 births during the June 1944 Red Cross visit.

findings.claim: Total arriving prisoner cohorts in Terezín (regular transports vs. including April–May 1945 evacuation transports)
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: Regular ghetto transports (Nov 1941 – Apr 20, 1945): ~140,000 (USHMM Theresienstadt, Yad Vashem, Památník Terezín, Beit Theresienstadt) to 141,184 (USHMM Bohemia & Moravia ledger). Adding ~15,000 concentration camp evacuation prisoners arriving in April–May 1945 yields ~150,000–155,000+ (Beit Theresienstadt notes up to ~158,000).

USHMM Bohemia & Moravia ledger gives 33,456 (USHMM Theresienstadt rounds to ~34,000); Yad Vashem gives 35,440; Památník Terezín gives >35,000; Beit Theresienstadt gives ~35,000 (~35,409). Discrepancy reflects regular wartime ghetto registry totals (33,456) vs. expanded postwar tallies incorporating late-war evacuation and typhus deaths at/around liberation (35,440).

findings.claim: Prisoners deported east from Terezín and survivors among eastern deportees
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: Deportations east: 86,934 (Yad Vashem Timeline), >87,000 across 63 transports (Památník Terezín), ~88,000 (USHMM Theresienstadt & Yad Vashem Ghetto article), 88,202 (USHMM Bohemia & Moravia ledger), up to ~90,000 (broader Yad Vashem summaries). Survivors among eastern deportees: 3,097 (Yad Vashem Timeline, matching Miroslav Kárný / Czech historiography), ~3,500 (USHMM Theresienstadt), ~3,800 (Památník Terezín). USHMM Bohemia & Moravia also records 16,832 liberated in Terezín, ~2,418 escaped/released earlier in 1945, and 276 arrested by the Gestapo.

myths_checked: EHRI unit https://portal.ehri-project.eu/units/cz-002195~pt-3941 is NOT a citation for 3,941 September 1942 deaths—it is an unrelated archival item (PT 3941, concert program in Heřman's Collection). The canonical EHRI source for 58,491 and 3,941 is https://blog.ehri-project.eu/2016/05/18/daily-orders-from-the-terezin-theresienstadt-ghetto/.
The 300–400 births figure reported to International Committee of the Red Cross inspectors in June 1944 was SS propaganda; documented births were 205–230 (207–230).
The 1,633 children (<15) liberated in May 1945 were not all long-term Terezín ghetto children—roughly half arrived on late-war April–May 1945 evacuation transports from other camps.

USHMM's 33,456 deaths and Yad Vashem's 35,440 deaths are not contradictory errors; they reflect regular wartime ghetto registry accounting (33,456 out of 141,184) versus expanded tallies including late-war evacuation/liberation-period deaths.
